recommendations.name: Han no Daidokoro
recommendations.reason: Onkee Korean Grill House was a 5 for you — tabletop grilling, good value, no wait — and this is the refined Japanese version of that same meal: A5 wagyu yakiniku grilled at the table with staff walking you through each cut. It also answers the one complaint that shows up again and again in your notes (Katsumidori 'interior is a little outdated', Roy's Ko Olina 'interior was outdated') with a genuinely polished modern room.
recommendations.avoids: The dated, worn-in dining rooms you flagged at Katsumidori Sushi Tokyo and Roy's Ko Olina; this is a new, design-forward space.
recommendations.dish: The wagyu course with the sukiyaki-style sirloin over rice and egg

recommendations.name: MW Restaurant
recommendations.reason: This is the upgrade on Roy's Ko Olina (4/5 — 'high quality, presentation was good, dessert was great, interior outdated'): same modern Hawaii-regional cooking and plating, a famously strong pastry program, but in a calm, contemporary room instead of a tired one. It also extends the Rigo Spanish Italian thread of a real kitchen doing careful, composed plates.
recommendations.avoids: The 'too noisy / music too loud' problem you docked Restaurant 604 and Monkeypod Kitchen for — MW is a conversation-level dining room.
recommendations.dish: The MW candy bar dessert, and the mochi-crusted local fish

recommendations.name: Mud Hen Water
recommendations.reason: The Kini Room got a 5 for mocktails, happy hour, terrace seating and atmosphere; this is the Kaimuki equivalent — an inventive non-alcoholic and craft drink list, small shared plates built on local ingredients, and open-air seating. It scratches the same 'good drinks plus interesting food in a room you want to sit in' itch, with the island produce angle Roy's hinted at.
recommendations.avoids: The loud-music, volume-over-food feel that dropped Monkeypod Kitchen to a 3; this is a small neighborhood room, not a party bar.
recommendations.dish: The 'ulu (breadfruit) dish and the kalua pig with greens

recommendations.name: Tonkatsu Tamafuji Kapahulu
recommendations.reason: Your two 5s and 4s in Japanese are both sushi (Ginza Onodera, Katsumidori) — what the notes actually praise is precision and freshness, not raw fish specifically. Tamafuji is the same obsessive Japanese single-dish craftsmanship applied to Hokkaido-style tonkatsu: pick your pork, grind your own sesame, exacting frying. A new slot rather than a fifth sushi bar.
recommendations.avoids: The 'food was ok, nothing amazing' middling-kitchen feeling of Restaurant 604; this is a specialist that does one thing extremely well.
recommendations.dish: Kurobuta rosu katsu set with the cabbage refills

recommendations.name: ‘AMA‘AMA – Contemporary Island Cooking
recommendations.reason: Keeps one pick close to home in Ko Olina so you are not always driving to town. It is the same bracket as Roy's Ko Olina (4/5, 'high quality, pricier side, would recommend') — contemporary island seafood, careful presentation — but with the oceanfront open-air setting and drinks program that made The Kini Room a 5 for you.
recommendations.avoids: The dated interior you knocked Roy's Ko Olina for; this room is open to the lagoon rather than enclosed and worn.

recommendations.name: Mimi's Peruvian Cuisine
recommendations.reason: Rigo Spanish Italian was a 5 and cino a 4, so Mediterranean-European flavor is clearly your lane; Peruvian is the logical unexplored extension — citrus-cured seafood and Spanish-rooted stews, with the Japanese-influenced tiradito style that connects to your sushi scores. It is a small family kitchen, so expect food over decor.
recommendations.avoids: The big, echoing, music-driven rooms that got Monkeypod Kitchen and Restaurant 604 only 3s — this is a quiet, small dining room.
